citations.narrative:
A nursing female and eight 4.5 week old puppies were in an enclosure that had mesh flooring. The openings in the
flooring measured 1.375 inches by 0.875 inches. The puppies were able to easily stick their legs through the flooring. I
observed the puppies tripping and getting stuck as they were trying to walk around the enclosure.
Mesh flooring that allows the puppies legs to pass through the openings can result in the puppies getting injured. The
licensee must either move the puppies to an enclosure where their legs won't pass through the openings or fix their
current enclosure so they are unable to pass their legs through those openings.
Correct by 6/14/26.

The facility has an exercise plan that was approved by a previous attending veterinarian, but there is no exercise plan that
has been approved by the current attending veterinarian. Exercise for dogs is critical for healthy development and
psychological well-being. The licensee must develop, document, and follow an appropriate plan to provide dogs with the
opportunity for exercise. In addition, the plan must be approved by the attending veterinarian. The plan must include
written standard procedures to be followed in providing the opportunity for exercise. Correct by 7/11/26.

citations.desc: Cleaning, sanitization, housekeeping, and pest control.
citations.narrative:
During inspection, I observed the facility representative move an adult dog into an enclosure that had fecal matter in it.
Not cleaning and sanitizing an enclosure prior moving a dog into it can contribute to the spread of disease. All enclosures
must be cleaned and sanitized before they can be used to house a dog(s). Correct starting on 6/11/26.

The facility representative reported that all the dogs are up to date on their distemper and parvo vaccines, but the date
those vaccines were administered has not been documented anywhere. Not documenting the date when the distemper
and parvo vaccines was administered doesn't ensure the vaccines have been given. The date the distemper and parvo
vaccines are administered must be documented going forward. Correct starting on 6/11/26.

The licensee has completed annual exams on all the dogs, but the documentation for the annual exams doesn't have a
date as to when these exams were completed. Without a date on the annual exams, there is no way for the inspector to
confirm when the annual exams were completed and if they had been completed in the past year. The dates and
findings/results of all screening, routine, or other required or recommended tests or examinations must be documented
going forward. Correct starting on 6/11/26.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the facility representative.
End of report.
